member.summary:
Milliseconds since the monitor thread last made forward progress (iteration boundary or pause-spin tick). Returns int.MaxValue if the monitor has not yet started. External watchdogs use this to detect a hung SCardEstablishContext after a PC/SC service restart and force recovery via Stop() + Start().
Cross-wraparound safe: unchecked subtraction on 32-bit Environment.TickCount produces the correct elapsed interval even when the TickCount wraps (every ~49 days of uptime).

member.name: M:AE.EmiratesId.IdCard.ReaderMonitor.Start
member.summary: Starts the monitoring background thread. Thread-safe -- concurrent callers serialise on an instance lock so only one monitor thread is ever created per ReaderMonitor instance.

member.name: M:AE.EmiratesId.IdCard.ReaderMonitor.Stop
member.summary:
Stops the monitoring background thread gracefully. Thread-safe -- concurrent Stop() / Dispose() / Start() callers serialise on the instance lock for the full Stop duration (including Join). This prevents a Start() from racing in between cancel-signal and thread-exit and resetting _stopRequested while the prior thread is still draining (which would orphan the prior thread forever).
Contract: subscribers MUST NOT call Start / Stop / Dispose synchronously from inside an event handler -- the monitor thread is invoking the handler, and Stop's Join would self-deadlock.
If the join times out (5 s), the orphan thread is logged via Trace. The post-Dispose event guard suppresses its events when the monitor was disposed, but on a Stop()+Start() cycle (where the monitor is re-armed instead of disposed) the orphan continues running until its next loop iteration; the per-thread generation counter then makes it exit. This leaves a brief window (up to ~CardChangeTimeoutMs = 2 s) during which two monitor threads may concurrently call PCSCLib's WaitForCardChange against the same SCARDCONTEXT. PCSCLib's state cache is not synchronised against concurrent callers (per its single-thread contract); the worst observable effect is spurious add/remove events that self-correct on the next clean tick.

member.name: M:AE.EmiratesId.IdCard.ReaderMonitor.Pause
member.summary: Suspends event processing without stopping the monitoring thread. The thread remains alive but does not make PC/SC calls or raise events while paused. Use for card operations that need exclusive PC/SC access. Thread-safe -- can be called from any thread.

member.name: M:AE.EmiratesId.IdCard.ReaderMonitor.Resume
member.summary:
Resumes event processing after a Pause. Cancels any active WaitForCardChange so the monitoring thread re-evaluates state immediately rather than waiting up to 2000ms for the current timeout to expire.
CancelReaderWaitNative returns an int status code. Discard it unconditionally -- a cancel that arrives when no wait is active returns CodeNotSupported (369), which is harmless.

member.name: M:AE.EmiratesId.IdCard.Toolkit.Log(System.Int32,System.String,System.String)
member.summary:
Writes a message to the toolkit's unified log file. Safe to call at any time -- before is constructed, after is called, from any thread. Fire-and-forget: never throws, never returns an error code.
If the loaded EIDAToolkit.dll is older than v3.0.6 and does not export the ToolkitLog symbol, this call is a silent no-op. Use at application startup if you want a signal about whether log calls will actually appear in the file.
The message is a pre-formatted string -- '%' characters are rendered verbatim, not interpreted as format specifiers. Format in C# using string.Format, $"..." interpolation, or any other idiom before calling this method.
Do not log PIN values, biometric samples, raw card APDU responses, session cryptographic material, or private keys. The unified toolkit log is an audit surface accessed by support staff; content written here must not contain PII or sensitive data.
member.param: (0), (1), or (2). Values outside this range are treated as ERROR by the native logger.
Short module identifier (e.g., "PaymentPage"). Appears as [EXT:module] in the log line. NULL accepted (renders as "?"). Recommended ≤ 64 ASCII characters.

Pre-formatted message text. NULL accepted (renders as empty string). Effective length limit is approximately 380 bytes after UTF-8 encoding; larger messages are silently truncated by the native logger.

member.name: M:AE.EmiratesId.IdCard.Toolkit.IsLogSupported
member.summary:
Returns true if the loaded EIDAToolkit.dll exports the ToolkitLog symbol (v3.0.6 or later), false otherwise.
Triggers a side-effect-free probe on first call (no log line is written). Result is cached for the lifetime of the process; calls after the first are effectively free.
Applications that want a startup diagnostic ("is logging wired up correctly?") can call this method. Applications that just want to log can call directly without checking -- silently no-ops if IsLogSupported would return false.

member.name: T:AE.EmiratesId.IdCard.ToolkitLogBinding
member.summary:
Internal binding for the native ToolkitLog export.
The probe uses kernel32!LoadLibraryA + GetProcAddress to determine whether the loaded EIDAToolkit.dll exports ToolkitLog, without invoking the function. This keeps IsLogSupported() side-effect-free -- no synthetic log line is written during the probe.
The probe runs once per process on first call to Log or IsLogSupported. Result is cached in a Lazy<bool> with ExecutionAndPublication thread-safety, so the probe executes exactly once even under concurrent first-call pressure.
Log defends at three layers against NULL inputs: 1. The probe result gate (no call if unsupported). 2. Null-coalesce substitution at this boundary ("?" / ""). 3. The native ToolkitLog body's own NULL check (landed in Stage 1).
